# Plan: unattended SPE rounds, starting with round 5

One default first. This message does not show round 4's numbers or proposals. So each r05 number below is written as a rule on top of r04's measured value. I will fill in the actual values from `spe/prediction-log.md` and `spe/predictions/r04-draft.yaml` before I save `spe/predictions/r05.yaml`.

## 0. Ground rules for the night

- The user's overnight message is the only new spec input. No other user input will arrive tonight.
- Approval: your approval of this plan covers r05. Rounds 6 and later will not re-enter plan mode. Each later round writes its plan to `spe/plans/rNN.md`. It commits the prediction before any harness work starts.
- The author field changes for r06 and later. It will read "Claude, autonomous under the user's overnight instruction of 2026-10-21, not reviewed by the user." I will not claim plan-mode approval for rounds you did not see.
- All commits stay local. I will not push, open PRs, deploy, or send anything.
- I will stage only files under `spe/`. Other working-tree changes stay as they are.
- Each round's Workflow script keeps the round number in one `ROUND` constant.
- Default caps, which I will log in `spe/spec/disagreements.md`:
  - Rounds: r05 to r08 at most, so 4 rounds.
  - Spend per round: 1.5 times r04's measured cost.
  - Spend overnight: 5 times r04's measured cost.
  - Clock: no new round starts after 06:00 local.
- Default match tolerance: ±5 percentage points for rates, ±20% for cost, and exact for counts. I will log this in `disagreements.md` too.

## 1. Steps in every round

| Step | Output | Commit |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Specify | Transcript, the rNN table in `spe/spec/spec.md`, and defaults in `disagreements.md` | `SPE rNN specify` |
| 2. Predict | `spe/plans/rNN.md` and `spe/predictions/rNN.yaml` | `SPE rNN predict: <one line>` |
| 3. Harness | `spe/evals/harness/rNN-workflow.js`, with all gates passed | `SPE rNN evaluate (harness)` |
| 4. Run | Launch the Workflow, then wait for its completion notice | none |
| 5. Results | Graded results and voided-trial log | `SPE rNN evaluate (results): <headline>` |
| 6. Learn | Prediction log, failures, round N+1 proposals and draft, README | `SPE rNN learn: <one line>`, then tag `spe-rNN` |
| 7. Check | Stop and halt rules in section 7 | none |

I will not start round N+1 until round N's learn commit and tag exist.

## 2. Round 5: Specify

- I will write `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md` with your overnight message, verbatim.
- I will add an r05 requirement table to `spe/spec/spec.md`:

| ID | Requirement | Source | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| R5-01 | Keep every r04 requirement that r04 passed | r04 table in `spec.md` | Same grader checks as r04 |
| R5-02 and on | One row for each r04 "Proposed for round 5" entry I adopt | "r04 Fn" or "r04 proposal Pn" | The code check named in the proposal |
| R5-xx | Run as many rounds as make sense, then stop | User: "as many as make sense" | The stop rules in section 7, checked after each learn commit |
| R5-yy | Commit after each SPE step. Never push. | The user's commit request and the way | `git log` shows the step commits. `git status` shows nothing pushed. |

- Rule for adopting proposals: I adopt a proposal if it targets a logged F-number, has a code-checkable test, and needs no decision that only you can make. I reject a proposal if it changes scope or what counts as success. Each choice goes into `disagreements.md` as a logged default with a one-line reason.

## 3. Round 5: Predict

Configurations. Each one changes one thing from C0.

- **C0 (control):** the r04 configuration, unchanged.
- **C1:** C0 plus the adopted proposal with the highest priority.
- **C2:** this depends on r04. If every r04 configuration passed everything, C2 is C0 with harder tasks or stricter graders. If not, C2 is C0 plus the second adopted proposal.

| Metric | C0 | C1 | C2 | Grader check | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Code-check pass rate (%) | r04 + 0 | r04 + half the points r04 lost to the targeted F-type | r04 − 10 if tasks are harder, otherwise the same rule as C1 | Schema-validated code checks | C0 does not change. Past fixes recovered only part of their loss. I will use full recovery instead if r04's log shows full recovery. |
| Judge pass rate (%) | r04 + 0 | r04 + 0 | r04 − 10 if tasks are harder, otherwise r04 + 0 | The judge rubric, used only where code cannot check | Proposals target code-checked failures |
| Voided trials (count) | 0 | 0 | 0 | Peek scan of transcripts | No trial should read graders, answers, or predictions |
| Grader selftest | pass | pass | pass | Oracle passes. Empty and wrong outputs fail. | The grader is unchanged, or it is fixed and retested |
| Cost per trial | r04 + 0% | r04 + 0% | r04 + 25% if tasks are harder, otherwise r04 + 0% | Workflow cost log | Harder tasks run longer. This number is an estimate. |

Every row starts as "same as last round". The yaml file will record `same_as_last_round` for each cell.

## 4. Round 5: Evaluate

- Gates before launch. If any gate fails, I halt.
  1. Grader selftest. The oracle passes. Empty and wrong outputs fail.
  2. Regrade r04 as a control. It must reproduce r04's numbers within tolerance. If it does not, I treat the grader as broken and halt.
  3. Dry run on 3 cells, one from each configuration.
- Workflow arguments: `ROUND = 5`, configs `[C0, C1, C2]`, the same trials per cell as r04, extra trials for split cells up to 2 times the base count, and the per-round spend cap.
- The script skips any trial that would cross a cap and logs the skip.
- The run ends with failure analysis and a completeness critic.
- Cost estimate, not measured: r04's measured cost times (3 divided by r04's configuration count).

## 5. Round 5: Learn

- `spe/prediction-log.md`: Metric, Config, Predicted, Measured, Same as last round, Verdict, and Closer. A "Which Why broke" section quotes each missed Why and names the wrong assumption. I will say plainly whether "same as last round" beat my predictions.
- `spe/failures.md`: one entry for each new F-type. A grader bug found after the run counts as a failure. Original and regraded numbers go side by side.
- I will add a "Proposed for round 6" table to `spec.md` and write `spe/predictions/r05-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
- I will update `spe/README.md`, commit, and tag `spe-r05`.

## 6. Rounds 6 and later

- Each round starts from the previous round's proposals and draft yaml.
- Each round reuses your overnight message as its transcript, labeled as carried forward. No new user words are added.
- Each round keeps the same structure as sections 2 to 5, with `ROUND` set to the new number.

## 7. Stop and halt

**Normal stop.** I stop after the current round's learn commit if any of these is true:
- Predictions have matched results for 3 rounds in a row. Matching r03 and r04 rounds count if the log shows they matched.
- r08 is done, or the clock has passed 06:00.
- No proposal is left that I can adopt without you.

If every configuration passes everything, the next round uses harder tasks or stricter graders. If I cannot make them harder without a decision from you, I stop.

**Halt now.** I halt right away for any of these:
- A spend cap is hit.
- An answer key leaked.
- A gate fails or the grader is broken.
- A decision only you can make.
- A needed change outside `spe/`.
- A commit or hook fails.

On a halt, I commit the finished work as `SPE rNN halt: <reason>` and start nothing new.

## 8. Morning report (in chat)

- One headline for each round, with its commit hashes and tag.
- The prediction accuracy trend: metrics within tolerance out of total, for each round. It will also say whether "same as last round" beat my predictions.
- Spend for each round against the caps, and any skipped trials.
- Open decisions from `spe/spec/disagreements.md`, listing every default I logged for you to confirm or reverse.
- A confirmation that nothing was pushed, deployed, or sent.
